articles.title: Congress promised to close the THC loophole. Our kids are still waiting
articles.summary: The Senate delayed a deadline to close the hemp-derived THC loophole, and Senator Pete Ricketts says America's kids are paying a tragic price.
articles.body: I served as governor of Nebraska from 2015 to 2023. My team delivered for Nebraskans. We cut taxes, made the government work better and defended Nebraska values. I also signed the Nebraska Hemp Farming Act into law. This bill allowed industrial hemp to be grown, harvested, processed and marketed in Nebraska. We took this step to align Nebraska state law with the 2018 Farm Bill. We also wanted to support our agricultural community. This Farm Bill federally redefined hemp. It removed it from the Controlled Substances Act and legally separated hemp from marijuana. This was a well-intended change. Hemp farmers argued their crop was a commodity. They said declassifying it would create new economic opportunities. Congress listened and acted. Our state followed. The results are drastically different from what we anticipated. This Farm Bill created a loophole that enabled nationwide sales of unregulated, manufactured THC. THC is a highly addictive and mind-altering drug. Bad actors immediately capitalized on this loophole. They manufactured and commercialized delta-8 and delta-10 THC drugs. They packaged these drugs to look identical to popular candies, sodas and chips. Then, they flooded the market with these drugs. They shelved them at gas stations, convenience stores and smoke shops across the nation. These drugs don’t have an age restriction. Now, our children and communities are paying the tragic price. CLOSE THE BACKDOOR DRUG PIPELINE THAT’S EMBOLDENING ENEMIES AND HARMING THE PUBLIC According to the Journal of the American Medical Association, more than one in 10 high school seniors have used hemp-derived THC products. Teens are still growing, and their brains are still developing. This causes addictions to form more quickly. Teens who use this higher-potency drug can develop dependence or addiction within months of first trying it. This is nearly double the rate of older adults. We know that THC drugs are increasingly linked to IQ loss and significant mental health issues. THC is linked to depression, suicidality, psychosis and anxiety. Allowing these drugs to stay on the market is a disaster. MARIJUANA USE RISES SHARPLY AMONG ONE GROUP OF AMERICANS, NEW STUDY FINDS Teens aren’t the only vulnerable population. Our young children have been impacted too. A 3-year-old and a 4-year-old in Omaha found and ate what looked like candy in their mom’s purse. They overdosed. The kids ate 1,500mg THC gummies that were branded identically to Sour Patch Kids. Thankfully, these children recovered, but they aren’t the only children who have made this mistake. In Virginia, a 4-year-old boy died after eating his mom’s THC gummies. There has been an over 1,000% increase in reported accidental THC poisoning for children under 5. The National Institutes of Health directly links this staggering increase with the rising availability of edibles that look and taste like candy. Candies mimicking commercial brands are rarely legally regulated or lab tested. A package’s total amount of THC can be spread unevenly. That means a single piece might contain an unpredictable amount of the poisonous substance. Here’s some good news. Nebraska’s Attorney General Mike Hilgers has cracked down on THC drugs. He is fighting back against an industry that preys on our communities. In Congress, a bipartisan group of senators voted to close the THC loophole last year. This vote gave the THC drug industry until November 12, 2026, to get in line with the new law. We gave this industry a full year. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Here’s the bad news. Today is November 12, and the loophole isn’t closed. In August, enough senators banded together to delay the deadline. That was a mistake. Today should have been the day that Congress officially protected Americans from deadly THC drugs. Today should have been a day to celebrate. Instead, we gave a multibillion-dollar industry more time to profit off hurting our kids and communities. As the Senate returns to Washington, we must ensure this loophole is closed once and for all.

articles.title: Zoe Kleinman: How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions
articles.summary: Zoe Kleinman explains how the man who built Nvidia from the ground up lost everything in a matter of days.
articles.body:
If I'd told you this time last week that Jensen Huang was about to leave Nvidia, you would not have believed me.

The man who co-founded this enormously successful AI chip company, working tirelessly to build it from the ground up and steering it through some disastrous times with endless energy and ruthless determination, has ultimately been undone by his own love life.

It's an extraordinary tale and a strangely old fashioned one for a tech firm with its sights set on the future.

It spawned a plethora of viral memes, seeing Huang as the man caught by the Coldplay kiss-cam with a married colleague , or singing along to George Michael's classic hit about betrayal, Careless Whisper.

Both were ironically AI-generated using the very tech he was helping to build.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits in wake of affair with suspected Chinese spy, as firm's stocks plunge

This week I met two Silicon Valley execs and I asked them how they were processing the news - "in memes", was the response.

But they didn't seem to think Huang would be forced out by his alleged adultery.

The stakes were too high, they said, the entire AI industry relies too heavily on Nvidia chips to break a winning formula.

In as many words, "the Valley" was on his side.

But that was before rumours of a second affair surfaced, this time with a colleague, and the board decided he had gone too far.

His behaviour suddenly cast him in a different light: a man who could make bad decisions and cover them up.

Huang always made a point of standing out from the crowd.

During the coronavirus lockdowns, he streamed keynote speeches from his kitchen (which gained internet fame in its own right, but were later revealed to have been AI-generated).

He is rarely seen without a leather jacket – he has joked that he only owns one suit, and he borrows his daughter's partner's tie.

Huang rubbed shoulders with the elite, with a network including Donald Trump, Elon Musk and King Charles.

The last time I saw him was at St James' Palace last year, where he was receiving the prestigious Queen's Prize for Engineering.

I was told he would not talk to the press - but he wandered over by himself and we spent about 10 minutes having a chat while press officers hovered nervously in the background. He was articulate and optimistic about the progress of AI and the UK's role in it.

For many people, Huang was Nvidia. He had as many as 200 people directly reporting to him.

He expected high standards – in his book about its inner workings, the Nvidia Way, author Tae Kim wrote the office hours were long

Huang's feedback could be both brutal and public, and he thought nothing of pointing out individuals' mistakes in all-staff meetings.

Now it is his own shortcomings which are on very public display, and he has been forced into a brutal ending of his own career.

Colette Kress, who takes over for now, will be a familiar face internally and that must feel reassuring to some at Nvidia.

She's worked at the firm for 13 years and for those who follow the firm's considerable finances, she is often present on earnings calls. She is a billionaire in her own right and a high-flying tech exec.

But she's not an engineer and Nvidia's products are highly technical.

She will have to convince investors that it is business as usual for Nvidia, that the innovation for which it is renowned can continue at its existing pace, and that the top talent won't leave with Huang.

A wobbly Nvidia would be bad news for the entire AI industry because its ever-advancing chips drive the most powerful AI models, and it's also regarded as something of a central bank, loaning money to other firms.

As for Huang himself, we assume for now that the investigation into his relationship with the woman accused of being a Chinese spy will continue, and the results of that may well determine what he does next.

He probably won't be short of offers despite his conduct – and I expect Nvidia's rivals can't believe their luck that their formidable rival has taken himself out of the game. Elon Musk has already said it would be "an honour" to work with him at SpaceX.

It's important though to remember that even if Huang turns out not to have betrayed his company or his country, he still betrayed his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang.

And for her, it's not a story of tech, temptation and trillion-dollar-valuations.

articles.title: Prominent Israeli settler denied entry into France
articles.summary: Israel criticises Yossi Dagan’s entry ban, labelling it ‘unacceptable’ amid tensions over illegal settlement policies.
articles.body:
The head of an organisation representing illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank has been denied entry into France.

Israel denounced the move as “completely unacceptable” on Wednesday after prominent Israeli settler Yossi Dagan said French authorities turned him back last week when he flew into a Paris airport.

Dagan, who is a member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party , was “subject to an administrative ban from the territory due to his active role in implementing the settlement policy in the West Bank” according to his office.

“Settlement building is contrary to international law and undermines the two-state solution,” the French ministry said.

According to the ministry, Dagan was “pulled aside and questioned” at the airport’s passport control before being informed that he was banned from entering French territory “due to his active role in implementing the settlement policy in the West Bank.”

Dagan said Wednesday that he was undeterred by the ban and was proud to “build the historic homeland of the Jewish people”, while Israeli’s foreign ministry said the measures against Dagan were based on “political and ideological grounds”.

“Israel will demand an explanation from the French government and consider its next steps accordingly,” it added.

The incident comes amid growing tension between Israel and European countries around illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank, which have proliferated under Netanyahu’s government.

France, along with 11 other countries, announced its intention to restrict trade with ⁠⁠⁠⁠illegal settlements in the Palestinian territory in September, which spurred outrage from Israeli officials.

On Monday, a French parliamentary committee approved a bill banning the imports of settlement goods and services contributing to settlement construction, with further discussion scheduled for November 19.

There are at least 148 illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank and 15 in occupied East Jerusalem, now home to about 750,000 Israelis, according to Israeli anti-settlement watchdog Peace Now.

Earlier this year, France banned far-right Israeli ministers, Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, who are both members of Netanyahu’s cabinet.

articles.title: 'I am under house arrest': Sonam Wangchuk speaks out against restrictions on movement in Ladakh
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has written to the Ladakh administration seeking clarification over a 60-day order restricting his movement,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has written to the Ladakh administration seeking clarification over a 60-day order restricting his movement, alleging that he has effectively been placed under house arrest without any formal direction or legal justification.In his representation, dated November 12, Wangchuk said the order issued by the office of the additional district magistrate, Leh, on November 11 under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) had curtailed his freedom of movement and speech. He also sought an explanation for the deployment of around 20 to 22 armed police personnel at and around his residence.“The practical effect of their presence is that I am confined to my house,” Wangchuk said, asking the administration to clarify in writing whether he was free to leave his residence and, if not, under which legal provision he was being restrained.He said the order did not explicitly direct him to remain at home or mention house arrest, detention or confinement. According to Wangchuk, police personnel had orally instructed him to stay at his residence after taking him there on Wednesday evening.Wangchuk said he was at the proposed venue of a dharna at NDS Memorial Park in Leh around 8pm on November 11 when a group of policemen arrived and handed him a copy of the magistrate's order. He alleged that he was forcefully pushed into a vehicle by four masked men and taken to his residence at HIAL, reaching there around 8.40pm.He further alleged that he was not allowed to use his phone to inform his family or speak to a lawyer. He said around 20 to 22 armed police personnel had remained deployed at and around his residence since then.The activist also questioned the scope of the restrictions, saying the order did not specify where he could travel, during what hours, or whether he could leave home for work, medical treatment, worship or family obligations. He said the expression “any activity” in the order was vague and could prevent him from carrying out his ordinary occupation and day-to-day activities.The representation also sought a copy of the letter from the Senior Superintendent of Police, Leh, on which the magistrate's order was based, along with the material facts cited to justify the restrictions.Wangchuk said a dharna had been planned for November 12 to raise concerns over the advancement of the elections to December 4, the stalled dialogue between Ladakh representatives and the Union government, and the delay in making public the judicial inquiry commission report into the September 24, 2025 incidents.He said around 600 people had gathered for the protest on Thursday and that it had passed off peacefully, with no objection from the police. He argued that the gathering had not been stopped despite the order restricting unauthorised rallies and public gatherings.Questioning the administration's justification for the 60-day restrictions, Wangchuk said the electoral process was scheduled to conclude on December 8 and alleged that the action was intended to curtail his rights before the elections.He asked the administration to withdraw the order and the police deployment, and provide written clarification on the legal basis for restricting his movement.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers
articles.summary: The proposals would change how crimes committed by children are disclosed to bosses in England and Wales.
articles.body:
Some job applicants in England and Wales would no longer need to declare criminal convictions they received as children under government proposals designed to improve the employment prospects of rehabilitated young people.

The changes would mean criminal records for people detained when they were under 18 years old would no longer show up for life during checks carried out by employers.

The Ministry of Justice has also launched a consultation on relaxing disclosure requirements for some specific drug-related and violent crimes committed by children.

Young people who have not re-offended as adults struggle to find work because of their past behaviour, the government says.

Many employers require applicants to undergo a background check, which in their most basic form require people to self-declare if they have a criminal record.

For more sensitive roles, such as working with children or joining the police, an employer can carry out a standard or enhanced check, which allows them to request information from the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS).

How long a criminal record must be volunteered for or will show up in those checks differs depending on the severity of the offence, the punishment received and how long ago the crime was committed - sometimes referred to as whether a conviction is 'spent'.

For example, a young person who was convicted and fined for an offence when they were under-18 will have that information show up in checks for five-and-a-half years. If they were given a custodial sentence, that will be disclosed for the rest of their lives.

The government wants to reduce the number of young people those disclosure rules apply to if an applicant has not continued to offend as an adult.

Five offences would be removed from a list of crimes which will show up in background for checks for life if committed by an adult. They are: affray, violent disorder, supplying a controlled drug to a child, robbery and assaults occasioning actual bodily harm.

Between March 2022 and March 2026, around 8,500 under-18s were convicted of those offences, according to Ministry of Justice data.

The government says that type of crime is often a result of peer pressure, exploitation and "adolescent impulsivity" by individuals who are still developing, as opposed to a broader propensity for crime and violence.

Under the new rules, they would cease to show up in checks after five-and-a-half years.

Lifelong disclosure would also be removed for offences which led to a detention period of less than two years, the maximum which can be handed out by a youth court, and replaced by a new 11-year disclosure period.

In cases where a child was given a sentence longer than two years - which can only happen if the severity of the crime meant they were dealt with by an adult crown court - the rules would stay the same.

The most serious offences - including severe violence, terrorism-related crimes and sexual offences - would be exempted from the reforms.

Cutting or removing altogether the disclosure period for offences which led to a fine, the majority of which are for driving-related crimes

Ending disclosure of offences which were dealt with via an out of court resolution, which have primarily been used to tackle knife possession and assault

Reforming how long earlier offences appear in checks for young people who committed more than one crime as a child

Announcing a consultation on proposals, justice minister Jake Richards said: "Many young people who offend do not go on to lead lives of crime.

"They take responsibility, turn their lives around and want to make something of themselves.

"When they do, we should recognise that progress and support them – not put unnecessary barriers in their way."

The proposals come as the government prepares to publish a long-awaited report authored by former Labour minister Alan Milburn on tackling the number of young people not in work or education .

In May, he warned the UK was at risk of a raising a "lost generation" as almost one in eight young people are not working or studying.

Richards pointed to that intervention as he announced the disclosure reforms, saying barriers to employment can be "particularly difficult to overcome" for people who committed crimes as children.

articles.title: Three UK school staff spent 25 minutes performing CPR on a cyclist who collapsed during their lunch break; a year later, Kip Knowles reunited with the women as they received national lifesaving awards
articles.summary: Kip Knowles, 58, has reunited with the three school staff members who saved his life last year, after he collapsed in cardiac arrest while cycling alone
articles.body: Kip Knowles, 58, has reunited with the three school staff members who saved his life last year, after he collapsed in cardiac arrest while cycling alone on the South Downs. PE teacher Stacey Charman, cookery teacher Chellie Messenger and school nurse Claire Agnew performed CPR for around 25 minutes and used a defibrillator to restart his heart. The women were honoured by St John Ambulance’s Lifesavers at Work Awards for their lifesaving actions, Sussex World reported. The charity launched the initiative to recognise inspirational lifesavers in workplaces across the UK. The event was held at Chapter Hall at St John’s Gate, London.“Every one of the winners was an ordinary person who refused to give up on someone whose life was slipping away. These people are alive today because someone nearby knew what to do, and that should be true for everyone in this country,” Shona Dunn, CEO of St John Ambulance, said at the event.“Cardiac arrest is the emergency that workers fear the most, yet two in five say they wouldn’t know how to perform CPR. That’s a gap we can close, and the workplace is where we can close it the fastest.“St John Ambulance has almost 20,000 volunteers keeping communities safe across the UK, but by training more first aiders in the workplace, we can create millions more lifesavers. Each of them takes those skills home to their family, onto the high street and into their community.”How three colleagues saved a stranger’s lifeIt was a regular afternoon. After lunch, Stacey Charman and Chellie Messenger were on a walk from Windlesham House School when Chellie’s dog, Waffle, led them along an unusual route. They saw a cyclist collapse on the road. The cyclist was Kip Knowles, 57, who had been riding alone on the South Downs. He had collapsed in cardiac arrest.They didn’t freeze. Stacey began CPR straight away. “Everything was a complete blur apart from Kip. I was in the zone, the training kicked in, and nothing around me could stop me from carrying on,” she told the outlet. Chellie wasted no time. She called 999 and used her walkie-talkie to radio the school for its defibrillator. Chellie was performing CPR on a person other than a training manikin for the first time. “It was horrible to see, but we didn’t stop. It wasn’t a case of ‘that’s it, he’s gone’. I was thinking – this man is the age of my husband,” she said.Soon, school nurse Claire Agnew arrived with the defibrillator. She has worked in nursing for 42 years and admits that her first thought was that Kip was dead. She delivered two shocks. “I thought he was dead. I know what a dead body looks like; I’ve done this for 42 years.” After roughly 25 minutes of CPR, Kip took a breath and sat up. That day, Kip Knowles got his life back. Exactly one year after the incident, he reunited with the three women as they were honoured with national lifesaving awards.The man recalls the dayKip had been in and out of consciousness before he stopped breathing altogether, and the team had kept going regardless. “I was on my bike in the middle of nowhere; I hadn’t seen anyone for hours. The ladies did CPR on me for around 25 minutes. I was going in and out of consciousness, and by the time Claire arrived with the defib, I’d stopped breathing, and they thought it was too late,” he told the outlet. Kip added that the three women had saved his life that afternoon. “But they didn’t give up on me, and I wouldn’t be here today without them.”Kip’s wife, Lucy, was the one who nominated the women for the award. “Our lives, and the lives of so many family and friends, would have crumbled had these angels not been there that day.”GP and broadcaster Dr Nighat Arif, who presented the award, emphasised the importance of immediate action in a medical emergency and how it can determine whether someone lives or dies. “As a GP, I know the minutes before an ambulance arrives can decide whether someone lives or dies, and the most important person then isn’t a doctor; it’s whoever is nearby.”“I’ve met people who used what they learnt at work to bring someone back to their family. I talk about health on TV, but what these winners did with their own hands is the most powerful message of all. They have demonstrated the greatest act of humanity in real life,” she added.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Best hiking spots in Eugene, Oregon, ahead of the Ducks' showdown with the Michigan Wolverines
articles.summary: Spencer Butte, Mount Pigsah and Salt Creek Falls headline the best hikes near Autzen Stadium ahead of the Oregon Ducks' home college football weekend.
articles.body: Trying to find a good city for both incredible hiking spots and some elite college football? Then Eugene, Oregon, has to be near the top of your list. Sure, the Ducks have sputtered a bit this season, but they are still in the thick of a College Football Playoff race, especially if they win out. They take on the Michigan Wolverines this weekend in Eugene, which means you have an excuse to make your way to one of the most scenic campuses in the country. The entire Pacific Northwest is breathtaking, and this week, we will identify a handful of the best hikes the Beaver State has to offer. Spencer Butte Perhaps the best all-around spot for a hike in the Eugene area (and that's saying something), Spencer Butte can offer a bird's-eye view of the surrounding locale before heading to Autzen Stadium for the game. The 2,058-foot peak is the highest point in Eugene's Ridgeline park system and will give hikers a panoramic view of both the Cascade Mountains and Coast Range. If you're looking for a challenge, try the West Trail, which offers a more demanding alternative, with scrambling and slippery rocks in wet weather. Any serious hiker has to put Spencer Butte at the top of their list, and the views alone are worth the trek. Mount Pigsah/Howard Buford Recreation Center If Spencer Butte is the most iconic summit in Eugene, Mount Pigsah is a close second. Offering over 30 miles of trails throughout the Howard Buford Recreation Center, Mount Pigsah features a 1,518-foot peak surrounded by more than 2,200 acres of oak savanna, meadows, riverside habitat and wooded slopes. WATCH: YOUNG BEAR TAKES ROUGH TUMBLE FROM DENVER TREE AFTER WILDLIFE OFFICERS TRANQUILIZE IT Hikers looking for a more strenuous adventure will definitely want to check the summit out, while those looking for a more leisurely stroll should stick to the Arboretum. That's the beauty of Mount Pigsah, there's something here for everyone. This is one of Western Oregon's best mountain views and it's just a few miles from campus. You couldn't ask for much more than that. Hendricks Park Our first two entries were a bit on the more rugged and elevated side, but if you're looking to be one with nature while taking things a bit slower, try Hendricks Park. Located just minutes from campus, the park allows you to walk among Douglas firs that are over 200 years old. It's one of Eugene's oldest parks, and the whole complex spans over 80 acres of gardens and forest. THE BEST HIKING AND OUTDOOR SPOTS NEAR FOLSOM FIELD FOR TEXAS TECH AT COLORADO GAME WEEKEND Hendricks Park offers a convenient and relaxing gameday hike that won't require a day trip, as you get to experience some of the emerald beauty of the Pacific Northwest without having to leave the zip code you're staying in. Wild Iris Ridge Park A hidden gem that offers incredible wide open prairie vibes, Wild Iris Ridge Park will have you questioning whether you're in Oregon or rural England. The trail offers a departure from some of the dense forests and buttes we've discussed so far, but that doesn't mean there isn't plenty of beauty to be seen. The park is home to over 250 acres of upland prairie and oak habitats that give way to views of the aforementioned Spencer Butte and the West Eugene Wetlands. The rolling hills are a sight to behold, especially with fall foliage, and the preserve is particularly interesting for anyone who enjoys birdwatching or native plant habitats. It's one of the lesser-known hiking destinations on the list, but the change of scenery and lack of tourists should be something that might pique your interest. Salt Creek Falls Consider this a bit of a bonus pick, since you'll need a full day to make it out here (but the trip is worth it). Roughly an hour and a half from campus sits Salt Creek Falls, which offers spectacular waterfall views poking through dense forests. At 286 feet, Salt Creek is the second-highest waterfall in Oregon, meaning one of the state's most breathtaking views is within driving distance for any college football fan staying the weekend in town. The observation platform is a stone's throw from the parking lot, and the additional trails offer other vantage points as well as a connection to neighboring Diamond Creek Falls. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP It's a drive, as I've noted before, but the facilities close in the winter, so if you have the time this weekend, I highly recommend making a stop out here.

articles.title: No breather: City air poor or worse on 11 of 12 days
articles.summary: Ludhiana’s air stayed poor or worse on 11 of 12 November days, with AQI hitting 275 and a yearly high of 314; officials cite weather and firecrackers.
articles.body: Ludhiana: There has been little respite for Ludhiana residents from polluted air this Nov. The city recorded an AQI of 275 Thursday, remaining in the ‘poor’ category and taking the number of days with poor or worse air to 11 in the first 12 days of the month.According to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data, an AQI of 201-300 falls in the ‘poor’ category and can cause breathing discomfort to most people on prolonged exposure.Nov 4 has so far been the only relatively better day this month, when Ludhiana recorded an AQI of 150, putting it in the ‘moderate’ category. On 10 of the 12 days, the AQI remained ‘poor’, while Nov 10 saw it deteriorate to 314, in the ‘very poor’ category.Thursday’s AQI of 275 was also the second-highest among the Punjab cities listed in the data, behind Bathinda at 328. Jalandhar recorded 207, Khanna 235 and Patiala 224. Rupnagar, at 42, had the cleanest air among the cities listed.The Nov 10 reading of 314 is Ludhiana’s highest so far this year. Over the previous two years, the city had touched 339 on Nov 2, 2024, while the highest reading in 2025 was 278 on Oct 22.PPCB sources said improvement in air quality would depend on favourable weather conditions, particularly rain or stronger winds that could help disperse pollutants. They also cited firecrackers as a major contributor to pollution.The prolonged spell of polluted air is beginning to tell on residents.Kuldeep Singh, a resident, said children and elderly people were particularly affected. Besides breathing discomfort, residents were experiencing a burning sensation in their eyes, he said.A homemaker from Dugri said she had stopped allowing her daughter to go outside to play in the evenings because of the polluted air. articles.title: Nirmal Kumar denies charges against TVK MLA, blames Kanimozhi for triggering controversy
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu law minister CTR Nirmal Kumar denies allegations against TVK MLA Arul Vignesh, blames DMK MP Kanimozhi; CM Vijay reviews law and order.
articles.body: Chennai: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay held a meeting to review the law and order situation in the state for the third consecutive day, even as state law minister C T R Nirmal Kumar denied allegations against the TVK MLA accused of sending inappropriate messages to a woman collector.After the meeting at the secretariat on Thursday, Nirmal Kumar accused opposition parties of triggering controversies, particularly DMK MP Kanimozhi for “levelling unsubstantiated charges” against Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh. “No such incident involving the MLA took place. Kanimozhi created an issue saying she came across such a message on social media,” he said when reporters asked whether Arul Vignesh had sent messages to the collector. “The issue has been amplified and wrongly projected in media,” he said. Anyone was free to contact those involved in the issue and verify the facts, he added.Nirmal Kumar said it was “not right” on the part of Kanimozhi to raise the issue. He refused to elaborate. “What I want to convey is that Kanimozhi’s social media post is wrong,” he said.On the charges that deputy speaker M Ravi Shankar assaulted a man who flagged a civic issue in his constituency, Nirmal Kumar said there were contradictory statements regarding the incident. An inquiry was under way to ascertain what had happened and appropriate action would be taken based on its findings, he said.He said govt had given the police department complete freedom to act. Referring to the crime situation, he said there had been 40 murders, including eight during the week of Diwali. “CM has taken all necessary measures to maintain law and order and prevent crimes. The police department stepped up drone surveillance as part of its crime-control measures,” he said.DGP Mahesh Kumar Agarwal said senior police and IAS officers attended the meeting and briefed Vijay on the law and order situation.Meanwhile, TNCC president B Manickam Tagore, who spoke at an event in Pudukottai, defended TVK govt.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chennai | Silver Rate in Chennai | Bank Holidays in Chennai | Public Holidays in Chennai | Chennai AQI | Weather in Chennai | Petrol Price in Chennai | Diesel Price in Chennai | CNG Price in Chennai | LPG Price in ChennaiStay updated with the latest Chennai news. articles.title: Six-day rural fair kicks off in Dimapur, brings together entrepreneurs & artisans
articles.summary: Six-day SARAS Mela 2026 opens in Dimapur, showcasing SHG and artisan products from Nagaland and four states, with workshops and buyer-seller meets.
articles.body: Dimapur: The six-day SARAS Mela 2026 opened at the Dimapur District Sports Complex Stadium on Thursday, showcasing indigenous products made by self-help groups (SHGs), rural entrepreneurs and artisans from Nagaland and four guest states of Manipur, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh and Karnataka.The mela, billed as ‘The Biggest Rural Fair’, has been organised by the Nagaland State Rural Livelihoods Mission (NSRLM).
